name: Night Drum
description: A tuned hand drum for every key, whose weighted skin has a true pitch: rolled with the fingertips into a breathing chord, struck, brushed, rubbed until it moans, or hummed into.

params.name: Hand
params.description: How the skin is played. The first four strike it. A brush swirls, a rubbing finger moans and a hum sings for as long as the key is held. Heard from the next key.

params.name: Place
params.description: Where on the skin the hand lands. The centre wakes the hollow, round modes; toward the rim the higher ones ring and the tone turns thin and clear.

params.name: Touch
params.description: How hard and short the contact is. Soft flesh wakes little above the note; a hard touch brings out the overtones and the hand itself.

params.name: Grain
params.description: How much of the hand itself is heard: the patter of fingertips, the slap, the bristles, the dry finger or the voice before it reaches the skin.

params.name: Roll
params.description: Strokes a second while a key is held, kept up at one level like a drum roll. At zero a key is one stroke. A brush swirls, a rub chatters and a hum shakes by it.

params.name: Scatter
params.description: How far strokes stray in time, strength and place, and how deeply the roll breathes. At zero every stroke is in step with the skin and the tone is still.

params.name: Swell
params.description: How long a key takes to rise. Short lets the first stroke be heard as it lands; long hides it and lets the drum come up out of nothing.

params.name: Load
params.description: How heavy the dark centre of the skin is. Bare, the overtones clash like thunder; loaded, they gather on the harmonics of the note and it sings.

params.name: Off Centre
params.description: Moves the load off the middle of the skin, which splits each pair of overtones in two, so they beat against each other. The note itself stays where it is.

params.name: Skin
params.description: What the skin is like, from thick and dull, whose overtones die at once, to thin and tight, whose overtones ring as long as the note.

params.name: Ring
params.description: How long the skin rings after a stroke, at the middle of the keyboard. The body and the hand shorten or lengthen it.

params.name: Damp
params.description: How much the other hand rests on the skin. It shortens the ring, takes the middle of the skin first, and stops the drum when the key is let go.

params.name: Bend
params.description: How far a stroke stretches the skin. Above zero the note starts high and falls back to the key; below, it starts low and rises. A steady roll bends far less.

params.name: Fall
params.description: How long a bent note takes to come back to its key.

params.name: Cavity
params.description: The body under the skin. A shallow frame is open and bright, a pot round and gulping, a kettle rings in fifths, a tube speaks like a vowel, none is dry and thin.

params.name: Cavity Tune
params.description: Makes the body larger or smaller: its formants and the air that rings in it go down or up, so the colour moves like a vowel while the skin keeps its note.

params.name: Other Skin
params.description: How loudly a second skin on the far side of the drum answers. It takes up what it shares with the first, and blooms after it.

params.name: Other Tune
params.description: The note of the second skin against the key. On an interval the two share overtones and it rings in sympathy; between them it is only touched by the strokes.

params.name: Snare Thread
params.description: A thread of gut laid on the skin. A little of it adds a soft buzz to the loud part of the tone; more lies closer, and turns a held note into a rattling drone.

params.name: Width
params.description: Spreads the two halves of the skin, the hands and the second skin across the stereo field.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. The modes are those of a round membrane (textbook Bessel zeros and shapes), drawn to harmonics as a centrally loaded skin does; the bodies and the hands are voiced by measurement and not taken from a particular drum. A mode is a rotating complex one-pole, the form modal-bells uses.
